output.brief: The remote promotion gap is mostly a difference in who was eligible, not evidence of bias against remote staff. Under the policy, people need 18 months in their level to be nominated. Only 32% of remote staff meet that, against 74% of office staff. Among eligible people, nomination rates are almost the same (28.2% remote, 28.6% office). Approval rates are also close (71% remote, 74% office). Eligible promotion rates are 20.0% remote and 21.1% office. Applying office rates to the remote eligibility mix predicts 8.2%, against 7.6% observed. The remaining gap of about one point rests on only 110 remote people, so it could be chance, and I can't rule out a small real effect. The dashboard's "every job family" pattern is likely the same tenure effect repeated in each family. I did not test the stretch-assignment concern or whether remote staff leave more often. Both are still open. Do not adopt the three-day office rule. It rests on a misread comparison and would hit about 180 remote hires on home-based contracts. Put it on hold. Change reporting to compare eligible people only, and re-check at FY2027. Meanwhile, look at stretch-work allocation and attrition. Confidence is moderate to high.
